body: Uh, what notifications?

There is `is_property_value_different()` method in PropertyUtils, I wonder if it should be used here? (it wasn't in the original code though, so not sure)

Same above.
I have the same impression, this was in the original PR

I tryed to understand the differences between this check and `is_property_value_different()`, Looks like `OP_EQUAL` is more relaxed and would allow type conversion (in example from Vector2 to Vector2i or float to int) while `is_property_value_different()` uses the `==` operator that would return false when type missmatches.

There are additional checks but are related to NodePath and Node/Array[Node] properties, which resources usually cannot have, so i think we can ignore those cases.

Someone with more insight could say which check is the correct one. From my point of view being strictier with `is_property_value_different()` makes sense

Most of the times, if you set a new base state, i'd expect properties of the object to adopt those values.

In the other hand, if undo/redo is buggy that's something we should look at indeed.

Should call `notify_property_list_changed();` ? if the base resource has a `script` assigned to it, or if hint_string of one property depends of another property, that could affect the behaviour of the inspector.

body: Added an additional note about return value

come to think of it, `set(E.name, p_resource->get(E.name));` should already be calling notify_property_list_changed
There's still one concern, that is what if the order in which properties are set leads to errors because it doesn't match expectations (in example you set a range value before setting min/max boundaries) i guess that's the reason why `_setup_inherits_state` exists, still ugly to think users have to deal with this manually, but i guess we can slowly fix error cases as they start appearing by overriding `setup_inherits_state` in each Resource class

> come to think of it, set(E.name, p_resource->get(E.name)); should already be calling notify_property_list_changed

Setting a property does not notify about property list, it needs to be done manually (because it's potentially expensive and sometimes causes problems if called too much).
Well yeah, something causes this property to get exposed in EditorSettings, which is why the doctool picks it. The bug is in whatever causes it to get exposed.
yeah, i meant the setter of one of the properties could be calling it

It's not guaranteed though.
And calling the method multiple times per frame is fine, because the update is queued.
